That skew is not a shortage of effort — it is a book of 19 open positions in a tape where the names worth owning are largely the ones already owned. Five ideas were researched and rejected with the arithmetic shown (ITB, the GLW/STX/NXPI group, BTC//MBT, NUE/SCCO, and an ENPH/GRBK/AWI small-cap pass), and seven watchlist entries carry triggers.

NOT TRUNCATED. Research ran 06:02-06:37 ET inside the pre-open window and closed with a RESEARCH COMPLETE block. Nothing here is reconstructed from a cut-off, and the research phase ran validate_report.py twice against throwaway copies before synthesis, fixing the first run's findings rather than noting them (hard failures went 30 -> 8).

TWO RECOMMENDATIONS ARE EXITS AND FAIL VALIDATION BY DESIGN. CEG (rank 20) and SNX (rank 21) are CLOSE-AT-MARKET instructions on open losing positions. Both fail check_stop_distance at today's volatility — CEG's published 250.00 stop is 1.35 ATR from entry against a 2.0 floor (its ATR expanded to 6.3% on five consecutive lower closes), SNX's is 1.78 ATR — and neither can be re-cut to clear the stop floor and the 2.0 reward-to-risk floor at once: widening CEG's stop to 2.0 ATR (239.41) drops its ratio to 1.47:1, and SNX's (240.36) to 1.86:1. Both also fail check_expectancy, losing money at their own stated hit rates (CEG 30% claimed against a 31% break-even, -0.05R; SNX 28% against 32%, -0.14R). That failure IS the finding, and it is why both are exits rather than holds. Raising either probability to clear the floor would be inventing an edge to keep a position this report wants closed. If --enforce demotes them to the watchlist, the exit instruction must survive the demotion: a reader who holds CEG and SNX needs it more than a reader who does not. Their stops are left as published rather than widened, because widening a stop on a position you are telling someone to close at market makes the advice strictly worse — the ATR floor is an entry-quality gate.

RATIOS CLUSTER JUST ABOVE THE FLOOR, AND IT IS WORTH KNOWING WHY. Nine of the 18 swing ideas recompute between 2.00 and 2.19 against a 2.0 floor (TLT exactly 2.00, GE and FCX 2.06, LULU 2.07, SNX 2.08, STLD 2.12, XLE 2.13, CEG 2.18, SMMT 2.19). That pattern is normally the signature of targets fitted to clear the bar. Here it is mostly the opposite artifact: these are previously published, already-open positions whose entries and targets are fixed by what was actually recommended, re-measured against today's higher ATR — the ratio drifted down toward the floor rather than being tuned up to it. It still deserves the reader's suspicion on the thinnest of them, and the two that drifted below a floor were turned into exits rather than re-cut.

TARGETS ABOVE THE 6.0 ATR SWING GUIDE, left as published rather than trimmed to pass: KHC 16.07 ATR, CVS 7.89, LULU 7.64, UNP 6.62, SMMT 6.18. All are open positions carrying the target they were published with; the realistic near-term part of each plan is in its scale_plan. KHC's is the extreme case and is flagged for re-cutting rather than silently kept.
